lots.guide_summary: Range from the two close entries only, both ASKING (US dealer retail, 1stdibs): AUD 273 for one Victorian Tobacco Leaf plate to AUD 610 for a clean set of six Copeland Spode plates in another pattern. No SOLD and no UNSOLD record for this pattern or a polychrome Copeland Spode set. Category-guide Hobart sales of plain blue and white Spode were $40 to $110 hammer (dropped from the guide, see dropped_entries). USD to AUD 1.4358 (open.er-api.com, updated 19 Oct 2026).
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry survives, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For context only (not a bid): Gowans blue and white Spode sold at about $25 to $55 a plate hammer (lots 417872, 423009, 400036), which would put six stained plates somewhere near $100 to $200 hammer if the pattern earns no premium, but that is a category guide, not same-item evidence.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark and pattern number read in the photo, but only one base is shown and there is no SOLD evidence for the pattern; the range rests on US retail asks.
lots.dropped_entries: Removed from the guide range and from SOLD (not the same item, category guide only): Gowans 417872 ($110 hammer, 2 blue and white Spode plates, photo checked: a view plate and a Chinese-style plate), Gowans 423009 ($95, 3 Spode display plates and pin tray; I checked the photo: blue and white Spode Italian, Tower and similar printed plates, not polychrome), Gowans 400036 ($40, one blue and white Copeland Spode plate), Gowans 400590 ($260, large Copeland Chinese Rose dinner set). All four API records opened and price and bid count match the researcher. Relabelled: the 1stdibs Jewel set (id-f_33053422) is now marked sold on the page but shows no price paid or date, so it stays ASKING, not live.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: six plates, all the same pattern (large blue leaf with red veining, pink and orange flowers, blue branch border, red-brown rim). Two plates (front left, back left) show brown staining or crazing discolouration in the well; red rim line rubbed in places; no chips or cracks visible at this resolution. Photo 2: one base with blue printed COPELAND late SPODE ENGLAND cartouche and red painted 2 over 6207 (enlarged crop reads 2/6207) with a small mark beside it. Only one base shown.
lots.condition: Used. Staining in the well of at least two plates, rubbing to rim enamel. Backs of five plates not shown. Size not stated.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the plate diameter? Do all six bases carry the same Copeland late Spode mark and 2/6207 number? Any chips, hairlines or restoration, and is the brown staining in the wells deep crazing stain or surface dirt?

lots.working: Keep: lowest close same-item SOLD in similar condition = $80 (Gowans 403493, scratched top). 80 / 1.22 = 65.57, round down to $65 (all-in about $79). Flip: likely resale = $130 (middle of the three close SOLD, 80/130/150). Less a 15% vendor commission at a local auction = $19.50, outbound postage $0 (bulky, buyer collects) gives $110.50. 110.50 / 2.44 = 45.29, round down to $45.
lots.confidence_reason: Form is clear and three close SOLD results were opened with photos checked, but there is no maker label to read and the veneer checking and dull finish put lot 338 at the weaker end of the comparables.
lots.dropped_entries: Moved from close to category guide and left out of the bid working: Gowans 424975 ($180, burr walnut Queen Anne revival china cabinet on carved cabriole legs, a better and different style) and Gowans 364179 ($170, light oak convex-glass cabinet, different timber and form). Gowans 398836 ($35, flat-front two-door cabinet), 382717 ($90, blackwood leadlight half-round) and 436216 ($140, leadlight corner cabinet) remain category guides only. All eight Gowans records were opened and price and bid counts match the researcher. Armitage past results: one WebSearch returned nothing indexed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: breakfront cabinet with stepped top over the centre, flat glazed centre door with cream bakelite-type pull, D-shaped curved glass ends, two curved glass shelves, mirror or glass back reflecting the room, four bun feet. Photo 2: close-up of the curved front stile with fine horizontal veneer checking and a dry, dull finish; key on a string tag in the lock; glass looks intact. No label or stamp visible.
lots.condition: Sound looking structure, glass intact in the photos, key present. Veneer checking on the front stile and a dull dry finish. Interior and back not shown closely.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is all the curved glass free of cracks and chips, does the key lock the door, is the back mirrored or plain, and is any veneer lifting or missing beyond the checking on the front stile?

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD, all Gowans Hobart, AUD hammer, premium extra: 13 complete Singer treadle machines on tables, $10 to $180 over the last 12 months (opened API records). Results split in two: eight at $100 to $180 (mostly closed drop-head cabinets) and five at $10 to $35 (mostly open-head tables like this one, 0 to 2 bids). No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in similar condition = $10 (Gowans 404459, open black Singer head on a drawered treadle table). 10 / 1.22 = 8.20, round down to $5. Flip: likely resale taken as $30, the median of the seven open-head Singer treadle results (10, 20, 30, 30, 35, 115, 130); the higher closed-cabinet results are a different presentation. Less 15% vendor commission ($4.50), outbound postage $0 (buyer collects) gives $25.50. 25.50 / 2.44 = 10.45, round down to $10.
lots.confidence_reason: Many SOLD results opened with photos checked, but the head's model plate and serial are not visible, so the 201 identification is inference, and condition and working order are unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: Left out of the bid working as category guides (not complete Singer treadle machines): 411867 ($30, ANA treadle), 386471 ($60, bare base plus parts), 398814 ($80, base with table, no machine), 426407 ($30, base table), 431193 ($55, base with Huon pine top), 370595 ($120, base side table), 375597 ($110, marble top on base), 423067 ($65, marble top base), 423974 ($105, marble top base), 370984 ($110, portable Singer 201K in a case, a different configuration), 381544 ($11, electric Singer head on a small side table, no treadle). All Gowans API records were opened and prices and bid counts match the researcher. Armitage past results: one WebSearch returned nothing from the Armitage site.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1 and 2: Singer iron treadle base (SINGER cast in the stretcher) with wheel and foot plate, oak table with two small drawers and a folding left leaf. No treadle belt is visible. Photo 3: black head with gilt SINGER flanked by small Greek-key style ornaments, hammered nickel faceplate, chrome spoked handwheel, motor mounted behind the arm, worn gold pillar medallion, heavily worn and dirty bed plate. No model plate, serial or cord seen.
lots.condition: Used and dirty, enamel and bed plate worn, no cord, foot controller or belt visible, untested.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the serial number or model on the head (to confirm a 201)? Is there a power cord and foot controller, does the motor run, and is a treadle belt fitted so it can be used by foot?
